title: Nurse-delivered alcohol screening and brief intervention on an acute psychiatric ward: a feasibility study
abstract: Objectives: to estimate screening, uptake, delivery, fidelity and three-month follow-up for nurse-delivered alcohol screening and a two-session brief intervention on an acute psychiatric ward, against pre-stated progression criteria. Design: single-ward feasibility study, January to September 2027. Results and conclusions will be written after follow-up.
introduction: Harmful drinking is common among psychiatric inpatients but rarely addressed during admission. Retrieved studies suggest nurses can deliver brief interventions and patients accept them once the crisis settles, while follow-up after discharge is difficult; trials in this population are few and mostly outpatient.
methods: Named nurses screen eligible admissions once the patient is well enough, offer two sessions before discharge, and complete fidelity checklists; nurses from another ward make three-month follow-up calls. Traffic-light progression criteria were stated before recruitment.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present the screening-to-follow-up flow, each proportion with its interval and traffic-light rating, fidelity, and session distress ratings.
discussion: The discussion will judge progression against the pre-stated criteria, describe who was missed, and state what the study cannot show about effectiveness. The planning value for delivery will be discussed only after its source is re-appraised.
limitations: One ward; observed delivery; phone-only follow-up; one planning value rests on a record whose identity check failed.
conclusion: To be written after follow-up; it will address feasibility and progression only.
reportingChecklist: CONSORT extension for pilot and feasibility studies (non-comparative items) with TIDieR
summary: Feasibility report draft with results left empty.
